# Comms Quick Reference
Exact controls, ranges, and modifiers for the field communications system.
For operating instructions, see [textlink="AN/PRC-117G Radio" link="AU14CommsANPRC"] and [textlink="Field Headsets" link="AU14CommsHeadsets"].
## Chat Prefixes
[bold]Prefix[/bold] [bold]Use[/bold]
[color=#a4885c]:h[/color] Headset default net.
[color=#a4885c]:v[/color], [color=#a4885c]:a[/color], etc. Other keyed headset nets. Examine the headset for available prefixes.
[color=#a4885c]:r[/color] Active AN/PRC memory.
[color=#a4885c]:x[/color] Headset direct frequency.
## Radio Training
[bold]GOVFOR and OPFOR:[/bold] Commander, Adjutant, staff officers, engineering officers, intelligence officers, synthetics, squad leaders, Fireteam Leaders, and Radio Traffic Operators.
[bold]CLF:[/bold] Cell Leader and Radio Operator.
Anyone who has read a [bold]field radio operator's pamphlet[/bold] is also trained. Handsets do not require training.
## AN/PRC Status
[bold]BIT[/bold] [bold]Meaning[/bold]
[bold]PASS[/bold] Powered, deployed, and on a working memory.
[bold]NO CELL[/bold] No battery fitted.
[bold]OFF[/bold] Set switched off.
[bold]STOWED[/bold] Powered and programmable, but not worn or deployed. No transmit, RADIO CHECK, SEARCH, or printing.
[bold]NO NET[/bold] No working memory selected.
[bold]SRCH[/bold] Search receiver active. Normal receive and transmit suspended.
[bold]OFF[/bold], [bold]CT[/bold], and [bold]PT[/bold] are fixed function-switch positions. [bold]LD[/bold] and [bold]Z[/bold] are momentary detents and spring back automatically.
The panel is worked entirely on the display. [bold]PRE[/bold] moves the cursor, [bold]ENT[/bold] works the line under it, [bold]CLR[/bold] backs out one screen, and the soft keys under the glass change screen. Text fields use the letter groups printed above the number keys.
## Coverage
AN/PRC figures below assume [bold]TX MED[/bold] and a whip antenna.
[bold]System[/bold] [bold]Clear[/bold] [bold]Degraded / Lost[/bold]
Named net through AN/PRC 0-30 tiles Degraded to 45; lost beyond 45.
Direct frequency 0-30 tiles Degraded to 50; lost beyond 50.
AN/PRC direct-frequency bridge Both users within 50 tiles Fails when either user leaves bridge range.
Command-post antenna mast 0-75 tiles Degraded to 100; lost beyond 100.
CLF relay set 0-35 tiles Degraded to 50; lost beyond 50.
CLF base station 0-55 tiles Degraded to 80; lost beyond 80.
Shipboard communications array Connected ship while powered No coverage when destroyed or unpowered.
CLF feeder tap Matches host mast or array Adds CLF nets without removing the host's existing nets.
Handset cord About 2.5 tiles Disconnects outside cord range.
Combat nets require coverage from a compatible relay source. Colony and civilian channels are not relay-gated.
## Net Splicing
A CLF Radio Operator can use a net splice kit to add CLF nets to a compatible mast or array. The host's existing nets remain active.
[bold]Target[/bold] [bold]Carriers[/bold] [bold]Probes[/bold] [bold]Open time[/bold]
Field antenna mast 2 24 6 seconds
Command-post mast 3 32 8 seconds
Communications array 4 40 12 seconds
- Probe signal reads zero more than 30 positions from a carrier. - A lock succeeds within 4 positions of the carrier. - Each probe adds 1.5% detection. - A missed lock adds 30% detection and consumes 2 probes. - Failure faults the junction for 90 seconds. - A feeder tap can be removed in 8 seconds. Removing it recovers its CLF keying module.

[bold]WHIP[/bold] Mobile or stationary 1x standard range.
[bold]MAST[/bold] Stationary About 2x while stationary; 0.5x while moving.

## Operating Modes
[bold]Mode[/bold] [bold]Function[/bold] [bold]Benefit[/bold] [bold]Cost[/bold]
[bold]FH[/bold] Frequency hopping Reduces jamming by one tier. 1.5x battery; small DF signature.
[bold]SC[/bold] Normal secured traffic No DF signature while secured. 0.75x battery; no jamming resistance.
[bold]CT[/bold] Cipher traffic between AN/PRCs Unreadable without matching fill; no DF signature while secured. Requires compatible fill-loaded AN/PRCs; no jamming resistance.
[bold]PT[/bold] Plain text 0.5x battery. Readable by compatible receivers; jamming increases by one tier; highest DF risk.
Matching COMSEC fill secures FH, SC, and CT. PT is always clear.

## Squelch
Squelch mutes degraded traffic; it does not improve signal quality.
[bold]SQL[/bold] [bold]Filtering[/bold]
[bold]0[/bold] Passes all traffic, including heavy static.
[bold]1[/bold] Suppresses heavy static and undecodable encrypted traffic.
[bold]2[/bold] Suppresses medium jammer degradation.
[bold]3[/bold] Default. Suppresses light jammer degradation and broken fringe traffic.
[bold]4[/bold] Maximum filtering. Weak long-range traffic may also be suppressed.
## COMSEC
[bold]Action[/bold] [bold]Result[/bold]
Insert matching fill Secures compatible FH, SC, and CT traffic.
[bold]ZEROIZE[/bold] Ejects the loaded card intact.
[bold]DESTROY[/bold] Permanently removes the loaded card.
[bold]RECRYPTO[/bold] Advances the faction's fill generation and makes older cards stale. Command authority required: Commander, Adjutant, or Advisor.
Captured current card Decodes compatible secured traffic from that faction until recrypto.
ZEROIZE, DESTROY, and RECRYPTO require a second confirmation within four seconds.
## Direction Finding
Signature-producing traffic, highest to lowest risk:
- PT traffic. - Faction-net traffic sent without matching fill. - Secured FH traffic.
Secured SC and CT traffic produce no direction-finding signature.
Higher transmit power and repeated qualifying transmissions increase detection risk. Direction-finding risk decreases after about one minute without another qualifying transmission.
## Radio Check
[bold]RADIO CHECK[/bold] reports which stations receive the active net clearly or with degradation.
When used inside a jammer field, it also reports a bearing to the strongest jammer.
## SEARCH
[bold]Property[/bold] [bold]Value[/bold]
Loaded nets All dropped while searching.
Transmit Inhibited.
Full band pass About 80 seconds.
Detection window Traffic within the last 20 seconds, within 60 tiles, on the same level.
Catches to resolve 4.
Partial-contact decay About 50 seconds without another catch.
Contacts below half confidence are hidden. Partial contacts show an approximate frequency. Full-confidence contacts reveal the exact frequency and net name.
## Net Log
The AN/PRC stores the last [bold]50[/bold] entries while powered. Traffic from another faction is marked [bold]INTERCEPT[/bold].
[bold]PRINT LOG[/bold] prints the full log. [bold]PRINT INTERCEPTS[/bold] prints only intercepted entries.
